text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Saturday's Pakistani newspapers: (Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy).
THE NEWS

- The government has scrapped a 6.2 billion rupee People's Tractor Scheme under which farmers were being provided tractors imported duty-free. This has been done at the request of the government's Central Board of Revenue.
- Former Afghan king Zahir Shah has decided to end a 24-year self-exile in Rome and return to his country in the near future.

- The State Petroleum and Marketing Company Ltd has terminated a joint venture agreement with the Crescent Refining and Marketing Company for the construction of a multi-million dollar hydrocracker project in Pakistan.
- White-fly attacks have been reported from urban areas of Multan administrative division in Punjab province because of rigorous sprays of pesticides in cotton fields.
DAWN

- The Mohajir National Movement (MQM) and its allies in the nine-party alliance will observe a strike in Karachi on Saturday to protest against the induction of a woman MQM deputy of Sindh provincial assembly in the cabinet.
- Palestinian President Yasser Arafat has supported Pakistan's stand on Kashmir and renewed his offer to mediate between Pakistan and India to resolve the dispute.
- At least 15 more people were killed in sectarian clashes between Shi'ite and Sunni Moslems at Teri Mangal and Kharlachi in the semi-autonomous Kurram Agency tribal area bordering Afghanistan.

- Leaders of militant Shi'ite organisation Sipah-e-Mohammad Pakistan has given a 72-hour deadline to the government for the arrest of the killers of the party leader Murid Abbas Yazdani, who was shot dead in Islamabad on Thursday night.
- The government has increased sale prices of petroleum product because of increase in oil prices in the international market.
THE NATION
- President Farooq Leghari told reporters in Kampala on Friday that India possessed a huge quantity of enriched uranium enough to produce 120 nuclear bombs.
- China has handed over to Pakistan compressor vessels for use at the Chashma nuclear power plant.

- Opposition leader Nawaz Sharif, while talking to reporters in Lahore on Friday, ruled out any overt or covert talks with the government, accusing Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto of adopting double standards.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- Commerce Minister Ahmed Mukhtar has said the volume of theft in revenue collection at various stages ranges from 30 to 90 percent, depriving the government of huge amount of revenue every year.
- A tractor assembly plant is being set up in Larkana as a joint venture between Pakistan and Romania in the private sector.
- Pakistan will hold a roadshow and meet potential buyers of a 26 percent stake of the state-run Pakistan Telecommunication Comany in October, a government consultant said.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
